newsitem.title: NORWAY: Cruise ship aground off Arctic island of Spitzbergen.
newsitem.headline: Cruise ship aground off Arctic island of Spitzbergen.

text.p: Norwegian coastguards said on Monday the Bahamian-registered Hanseatic cruise liner had run aground in a fjord off the north coast of the Arctic island of Spitzbergen.

The ship, with 145 passangers on board and a crew of 115, ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord but was in no imminent danger, said Arne Gansnoe, duty officer for the rescue centre at Bodoe in northern Norway.

"There is no critical situation. The passengers and crew are staying on board. Another ship is alongside her and a couple of naval vessels are heading out there to pull her free. There should be no problem if the weather stays fine," Gansnoe told Reuters.

The Norwegian national news agency NTB said the 9,000 deadweight tonne vessel was owned by Hanseatic Tours, a subsidiary of Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd Cruiseshipping GmbH. The coastguard could not confirm this.
There was no immediate information on how the vessel had run aground.

A Swedish passenger ship, Origo, had unsuccessfully tried to pull the Hanseatic free and was waiting alongside, the coastguard said. The first naval vessel was expected to reach the grounded ship at 1000 GMT on Monday.
"The situation is under control. If it had been criticl we would have started a rescue operation straight away," Gansnoe said.
NTB said the Finnish-built Hanseatic had run aground last August off the Canadian coast in the Arctic with 268 people on board.
